title: Plans: want to, have to, may
title_target: នឹង ចង់ ត្រូវ — neng, chang, treuw
goal: Talk about plans and obligations with five helper words that sit before the verb — with no change of form at all.
bekal: express obligation with ត្រូវ and "no need" with មិនត្រូវ
make suggestions with … ទៅ and … ចុះ

dialogs.title: កិច្ចសន្ទនា — Planning a trip to Siem Reap
dialogs.intro: Sokha, Sreymom, and Ani sit down to plan a trip. Notice that all the helper words — នឹង, ចង់, ត្រូវ, អាច — stand **before** the verb and never change form, no matter who is doing it.

lines.speaker: សុខា:
lines.text: [ថ្ងៃ|thngay] [សៅរ៍|saw] [យើង|yeung] [នឹង|neng] [ចេញ|cheñ] [ម៉ោង|maong] [ប្រាំមួយ|pram-muèy] [ព្រឹក|preuk] [បាទ|baat]។
lines.id: On Saturday we'll leave at six in the morning.
lines.literal: day — Saturday — we — will — go-out — o'clock — five-one — morning — yes(m).

lines.speaker: អានី:
lines.text: [យើង|yeung] [ត្រូវ|treuw] [ទិញ|teñ] [សំបុត្រ|sam-bot] [មុន|mun] [ទេ|té] [ចាស|chaah]?
lines.id: Do we have to buy tickets first?
lines.literal: we — must — buy — ticket — first — (question) — yes(f)?

lines.speaker: សុខា:
lines.text: [ត្រូវ|treuw] [បាទ|baat]។ [ថ្ងៃនេះ|thngay nih] [ខ្ញុំ|khnyom] [នឹង|neng] [ទៅ|teuw] [ទិញ|teñ]។
lines.id: We do. I'll go and buy them today.
lines.literal: must — yes(m). today — I — will — go — buy.

lines.speaker: ស្រីមុំ:
lines.text: [ខ្ញុំ|khnyom] [ចង់|chang] [ទៅ|teuw] [មើល|meul] [ព្រះអាទិត្យ|preah-'aa-tit] [រះ|reah] [នៅ|neuw] [អង្គរ|'ang-kaa] [ចាស|chaah]។
lines.id: I want to see the sunrise at Angkor.
lines.literal: I — want — go — see — holy-sun — rise — at — Angkor — yes(f).

lines.speaker: អានី:
lines.text: [ព្រះអាទិត្យ|preah-'aa-tit] [រះ|reah] [ម៉ោង|maong] [ប៉ុន្មាន|pon-maan] [ចាស|chaah]?
lines.id: What time does the sun come up?

lines.speaker: សុខា:
lines.text: [ប្រហែល|pra-hael] [ម៉ោង|maong] [ប្រាំ|pram] [កន្លះ|kan-lah] [បាទ|baat]។ [យើង|yeung] [ត្រូវ|treuw] [ក្រោក|kraok] [ម៉ោង|maong] [បួន|buèn]។
lines.id: Around half past five. We have to get up at four.
lines.literal: about — o'clock — five — half — yes(m). we — must — rise — o'clock — four.

lines.speaker: អានី:
lines.text: [ព្រឹក|preuk] [ណាស់|nah]! [ប៉ុន្តែ|pon-tae] [ខ្ញុំ|khnyom] [អាច|'aach] [ក្រោក|kraok] [បាន|baan] [ចាស|chaah]។
lines.id: That's early! But I can manage.
lines.literal: morning — very! but — I — able — rise — get — yes(f).

lines.speaker: ស្រីមុំ:
lines.text: [បើ|baeu] [ភ្លៀង|phlièng] [ធ្លាក់|thleak], [យើង|yeung] [នឹង|neng] [ធ្វើ|thweu] [យ៉ាងម៉េច|yaang-méch] [ចាស|chaah]?
lines.id: If it rains, what will we do?
lines.literal: if — rain — fall, we — will — do — how — yes(f)?

lines.speaker: សុខា:
lines.text: [បើ|baeu] [ភ្លៀង|phlièng], [យើង|yeung] [ទៅ|teuw] [សារមន្ទីរ|saa-rò-mon-tii] [ជំនួស|chum-nuèh] [បាទ|baat]។
lines.id: If it rains, we'll go to the museum instead.
lines.literal: if — rain, we — go — museum — instead — yes(m).

lines.speaker: អានី:
lines.text: [ខ្ញុំ|khnyom] [មិន|min] [ចង់|chang] [ដើរ|daeu] [ច្រើន|chraeun] [ពេក|péék] [ចាស|chaah]។ [ជើង|cheung] [ខ្ញុំ|khnyom] [ឈឺ|chheu]។
lines.id: I don't want to walk too much. My feet hurt.
lines.literal: I — not — want — walk — much — too — yes(f). foot — I — hurt.

lines.speaker: សុខា:
lines.text: [អញ្ចឹង|'añ-cheung] [យើង|yeung] [ជួល|chuèl] [ទុកទុក|tuk-tuk] [ចុះ|choh]។ [មិន|min] [ត្រូវ|treuw] [ដើរ|daeu] [ទេ|té]។
lines.id: In that case, let's just rent a tuk-tuk. No need to walk.
lines.literal: so — we — rent — tuk-tuk — then. not — must — walk — no.

lines.speaker: អានី:
lines.text: [ល្អ|l'aa] [ណាស់|nah]! [ទៅ|teuw] [ទិញ|teñ] [សំបុត្រ|sam-bot] [ទៅ|teuw]!
lines.id: Great! Let's go buy the tickets!
lines.literal: good — very! go — buy — ticket — let's!

grammars.title: Five helper words that stand in front
body: Khmer puts every helper word **before the verb**, and none of them ever changes form for anyone. English has *can, could, will, would, must, have to*, each with its own rules — here it's all one pattern.

head: Word
Say it
Meaning
Example
rows: ខ្ញុំនឹងទៅ — I will go
ខ្ញុំចង់ទៅ — I want to go
ខ្ញុំត្រូវទៅ — I have to go
ខ្ញុំអាចទៅបាន — I can go
ខ្ញុំគួរទៅ — I should go
ខ្ញុំចេះបើក — I can drive

after: Negation works exactly as in Unit 4: **មិន** goes before the helper word, **ទេ** at the end of the sentence. ខ្ញុំមិនចង់ទៅទេ (I don't want to go), ខ្ញុំមិនត្រូវទៅទេ (I don't need to go).
⚠️ Careful with **មិនត្រូវ**: it means "don't need to", not "must not". For "must not", use **មិនបានទេ** or **កុំ**. Getting this wrong can make a ban sound like a free pass.

grammars.title: ⚠️ នឹង is optional — and often left out
body: Just like បាន in Unit 12, នឹង is **not** a required tense marker. If your sentence already has a future time word, នឹង is usually dropped.

head: Khmer
Say it
Meaning
Note
rows: ស្អែកខ្ញុំទៅ
ស្អែកខ្ញុំនឹងទៅ
ខ្ញុំនឹងទៅ
នឹង used because there's no time word
now or later — depends on context

after: English does the same with "I'm leaving tomorrow", which sounds more natural than "tomorrow I will leave". Khmer feels exactly the same way. **If there's a time word, drop នឹង.**

grammars.title: Suggestions: … ទៅ, … ចុះ, and … គ្នា
body: Khmer has three ways to make a suggestion, and all of them use a little word at the **end** of the sentence — where English might put "…then" or "…OK?".

head: Khmer
Say it
Meaning
Feel
rows: ទៅញ៉ាំបាយទៅ
ជួលទុកទុកចុះ
យើងទៅជាមួយគ្នា

after: ⚠️ Look at the first sentence: ទៅ appears twice — once as the verb "go", once as the urging word at the end. This is no typo, and Cambodians say it this way every day. **តោះ!** is what you'll hear most from friends your age — it's exactly "let's go!" or "come on!".

blocks.text: បើ (*baeu*) means "if", and the order is just like English: **condition first, result second**. No verb changes, no special conditional forms.

head: Khmer
Say it
English
rows: បើភ្លៀង យើងមិនទៅទេ
If it rains, we won't go.
បើបងទំនេរ មកផ្ទះខ្ញុំ
If you're free, come over to my house.
បើថ្លៃពេក កុំទិញ
If it's too expensive, don't buy it.
បើអត់មាន ក៏អត់អីទេ
If there isn't any, that's OK too.

head: Khmer
Say it
English
rows: រថយន្តក្រុង
ព្រះអាទិត្យរះ
ព្រះអាទិត្យលិច

blocks.title: ⚠️ ព្រះ — a little word that marks something revered
items: **ព្រះ (*preah*) means "holy, revered"** and goes before things that are honored: ព្រះអាទិត្យ (the sun), ព្រះច័ន្ទ (the moon), ព្រះពុទ្ធ (the Buddha), ព្រះមហាក្សត្រ (the king), ព្រះវិហារ (a temple, place of worship).
It comes from Sanskrit, and you'll meet its relatives across Southeast Asia — Thai พระ (*phra*), for instance, in royal and religious titles.
At A1 you don't need to use it yourself — just recognize it, so ព្រះអាទិត្យ doesn't sound like two unrelated words.

exercises.prompt: Fill in with នឹង, ចង់, ត្រូវ, or អាច.
items: ខ្ញុំ____ទៅសៀមរាប។ (want to)
យើង____ទិញសំបុត្រមុន។ (have to)
ស្អែកខ្ញុំ____ចេញម៉ោងប្រាំមួយ។ (will)
ខ្ញុំ____ក្រោកម៉ោងបួនបាន។ (able to)
ខ្ញុំចង់ទៅ។
ខ្ញុំត្រូវដើរ។
ខ្ញុំនឹងទិញ។
ខ្ញុំចេះបើកឡាន។

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.
items: ទៅ / យើង / សំបុត្រ / ទិញ / ទៅ
យើងមិនទៅទេ / ភ្លៀង / បើ
ចុះ / ជួល / ទុកទុក
បាន / ខ្ញុំ / ក្រោក / អាច
I'm going to Siem Reap tomorrow.
We have to buy tickets first.
I want to see the sunrise.
If it rains, we won't go.
I don't want to walk too far.
Let's go!

answers: ចង់ — ត្រូវ — នឹង — អាច
ខ្ញុំមិនចង់ទៅទេ។ — ខ្ញុំមិនត្រូវដើរទេ។ — ខ្ញុំមិននឹងទិញទេ។ — ខ្ញុំមិនចេះបើកឡានទេ។
យើងទៅទិញសំបុត្រទៅ។ — បើភ្លៀង យើងមិនទៅទេ។ — ជួលទុកទុកចុះ។ — ខ្ញុំអាចក្រោកបាន។
ស្អែកខ្ញុំទៅសៀមរាប។ — យើងត្រូវទិញសំបុត្រមុន។ — ខ្ញុំចង់មើលព្រះអាទិត្យរះ។ — បើភ្លៀង យើងមិនទៅទេ។ — ខ្ញុំមិនចង់ដើរឆ្ងាយពេកទេ។ — តោះ!
